NASB.1: Guard your steps as you go to the house of God and draw near to listen rather than to offer the sacrifice of fools; for they do not know they are doing evil.
NASB.2: Do not be hasty in word or impulsive in thought to bring up a matter in the presence of God. For God is in heaven and you are on the earth; therefore let your words be few.
NASB.3: For the dream comes through much effort and the voice of a fool through many words.
NASB.4: When you make a vow to God, do not be late in paying it; for [He takes] no delight in fools. Pay what you vow!
NASB.5: It is better that you should not vow than that you should vow and not pay.
NASB.6: Do not let your speech cause you to sin and do not say in the presence of the messenger [of God] that it was a mistake. Why should God be angry on account of your voice and destroy the work of your hands?
NASB.7: For in many dreams and in many words there is emptiness. Rather, fear God.
NASB.8: If you see oppression of the poor and denial of justice and righteousness in the province, do not be shocked at the sight; for one official watches over another official, and there are higher officials over them.
NASB.9: After all, a king who cultivates the field is an advantage to the land.
NASB.10: He who loves money will not be satisfied with money, nor he who loves abundance [with its] income. This too is vanity.
NASB.11: When good things increase, those who consume them increase. So what is the advantage to their owners except to look on?
NASB.12: The sleep of the working man is pleasant, whether he eats little or much; but the full stomach of the rich man does not allow him to sleep.
NASB.13: There is a grievous evil [which] I have seen under the sun: riches being hoarded by their owner to his hurt.
NASB.14: When those riches were lost through a bad investment and he had fathered a son, then there was nothing to support him.
NASB.15: As he had come naked from his mother's womb, so will he return as he came. He will take nothing from the fruit of his labor that he can carry in his hand.
NASB.16: This also is a grievous evil-- exactly as a man is born, thus will he die. So what is the advantage to him who toils for the wind?
NASB.17: Throughout his life [he] also eats in darkness with great vexation, sickness and anger.
NASB.18: Here is what I have seen to be good and fitting: to eat, to drink and enjoy oneself in all one's labor in which he toils under the sun [during] the few years of his life which God has given him; for this is his reward.
NASB.19: Furthermore, as for every man to whom God has given riches and wealth, He has also empowered him to eat from them and to receive his reward and rejoice in his labor; this is the gift of God.
NASB.20: For he will not often consider the years of his life, because God keeps him occupied with the gladness of his heart.

ESV.1: Guard your steps when you go to the house of God. To draw near to listen is better than to offer the sacrifice of fools, for they do not know that they are doing evil.
ESV.2: Be not rash with your mouth, nor let your heart be hasty to utter a word before God, for God is in heaven and you are on earth. Therefore let your words be few.
ESV.3: For a dream comes with much business, and a fool's voice with many words.
ESV.4: When you vow a vow to God, do not delay paying it, for he has no pleasure in fools. Pay what you vow.
ESV.5: It is better that you should not vow than that you should vow and not pay.
ESV.6: Let not your mouth lead you  into sin, and do not say before the messenger  that it was a mistake. Why should God be angry at your voice and destroy the work of your hands?
ESV.7: For when dreams increase and words grow many, there is vanity;  but  God is the one you must fear.
ESV.8: If you see in a province the oppression of the poor and the violation of justice and righteousness, do not be amazed at the matter, for the high official is watched by a higher, and there are yet higher ones over them.
ESV.9: But this is gain for a land in every way: a king committed to cultivated fields.
ESV.10: He who loves money will not be satisfied with money, nor he who loves wealth with his income; this also is vanity.
ESV.11: When goods increase, they increase who eat them, and what advantage has their owner but to see them with his eyes?
ESV.12: Sweet is the sleep of a laborer, whether he eats little or much, but the full stomach of the rich will not let him sleep.
ESV.13: There is a grievous evil that I have seen under the sun: riches were kept by their owner to his hurt,
ESV.14: and those riches were lost in a bad venture. And he is father of a son, but he has nothing in his hand.
ESV.15: As he came from his mother's womb he shall go again, naked as he came, and shall take nothing for his toil that he may carry away in his hand.
ESV.16: This also is a grievous evil: just as he came, so shall he go, and what gain is there to him who toils for the wind?
ESV.17: Moreover, all his days he eats in darkness in much vexation and sickness and anger.
ESV.18: Behold, what I have seen to be good and fitting is to eat and drink and find enjoyment  in all the toil with which one toils under the sun the few days of his life that God has given him, for this is his lot.
ESV.19: Everyone also to whom God has given wealth and possessions and power to enjoy them, and to accept his lot and rejoice in his toil — this is the gift of God.
ESV.20: For he will not much remember the days of his life because God keeps him occupied with joy in his heart.

NKJV.1: Walk prudently when you go to the house of God; and draw near to hear rather than to give the sacrifice of fools, for they do not know that they do evil.
NKJV.2: Do not be rash with your mouth, And let not your heart utter anything hastily before God. For God is in heaven, and you on earth; Therefore let your words be few.
NKJV.3: For a dream comes through much activity, And a fool’s voice is known by his many words.
NKJV.4: When you make a vow to God, do not delay to pay it; For He has no pleasure in fools. Pay what you have vowed—
NKJV.5: Better not to vow than to vow and not pay.
NKJV.6: Do not let your mouth cause your flesh to sin, nor say before the messenger of God that it was an error. Why should God be angry at your excuse and destroy the work of your hands?
NKJV.7: For in the multitude of dreams and many words there is also vanity. But fear God.
NKJV.8: If you see the oppression of the poor, and the violent perversion of justice and righteousness in a province, do not marvel at the matter; for high official watches over high official, and higher officials are over them.
NKJV.9: Moreover the profit of the land is for all; even the king is served from the field.
NKJV.10: He who loves silver will not be satisfied with silver; Nor he who loves abundance, with increase. This also is vanity.
NKJV.11: When goods increase, They increase who eat them; So what profit have the owners Except to see them with their eyes?
NKJV.12: The sleep of a laboring man is sweet, Whether he eats little or much; But the abundance of the rich will not permit him to sleep.
NKJV.13: There is a severe evil which I have seen under the sun: Riches kept for their owner to his hurt.
NKJV.14: But those riches perish through misfortune; When he begets a son, there is nothing in his hand.
NKJV.15: As he came from his mother’s womb, naked shall he return, To go as he came; And he shall take nothing from his labor Which he may carry away in his hand.
NKJV.16: And this also is a severe evil— Just exactly as he came, so shall he go. And what profit has he who has labored for the wind?
NKJV.17: All his days he also eats in darkness, And he has much sorrow and sickness and anger.
NKJV.18: Here is what I have seen: It is good and fitting for one to eat and drink, and to enjoy the good of all his labor in which he toils under the sun all the days of his life which God gives him; for it is his heritage.
NKJV.19: As for every man to whom God has given riches and wealth, and given him power to eat of it, to receive his heritage and rejoice in his labor—this is the gift of God.
NKJV.20: For he will not dwell unduly on the days of his life, because God keeps him busy with the joy of his heart.

NLT.1: As you enter the house of God, keep your ears open and your mouth shut. It is evil to make mindless offerings to God.
NLT.2: Don’t make rash promises, and don’t be hasty in bringing matters before God. After all, God is in heaven, and you are here on earth. So let your words be few.
NLT.3: Too much activity gives you restless dreams; too many words make you a fool.
NLT.4: When you make a promise to God, don’t delay in following through, for God takes no pleasure in fools. Keep all the promises you make to him.
NLT.5: It is better to say nothing than to make a promise and not keep it.
NLT.6: Don’t let your mouth make you sin. And don’t defend yourself by telling the Temple messenger that the promise you made was a mistake. That would make God angry, and he might wipe out everything you have achieved.
NLT.7: Talk is cheap, like daydreams and other useless activities. Fear God instead.
NLT.8: Don’t be surprised if you see a poor person being oppressed by the powerful and if justice is being miscarried throughout the land. For every official is under orders from higher up, and matters of justice get lost in red tape and bureaucracy.
NLT.9: Even the king milks the land for his own profit!
NLT.10: Those who love money will never have enough. How meaningless to think that wealth brings true happiness!
NLT.11: The more you have, the more people come to help you spend it. So what good is wealth — except perhaps to watch it slip through your fingers!
NLT.12: People who work hard sleep well, whether they eat little or much. But the rich seldom get a good night’s sleep.
NLT.13: There is another serious problem I have seen under the sun. Hoarding riches harms the saver.
NLT.14: Money is put into risky investments that turn sour, and everything is lost. In the end, there is nothing left to pass on to one’s children.
NLT.15: We all come to the end of our lives as naked and empty-handed as on the day we were born. We can’t take our riches with us.
NLT.16: And this, too, is a very serious problem. People leave this world no better off than when they came. All their hard work is for nothing — like working for the wind.
NLT.17: Throughout their lives, they live under a cloud — frustrated, discouraged, and angry.
NLT.18: Even so, I have noticed one thing, at least, that is good. It is good for people to eat, drink, and enjoy their work under the sun during the short life God has given them, and to accept their lot in life.
NLT.19: And it is a good thing to receive wealth from God and the good health to enjoy it. To enjoy your work and accept your lot in life — this is indeed a gift from God.
NLT.20: God keeps such people so busy enjoying life that they take no time to brood over the past.

WEB.1: Guard your steps when you go to God’s house; for to draw near to listen is better than to give the sacrifice of fools, for they don’t know that they do evil.
WEB.2: Don’t be rash with your mouth, and don’t let your heart be hasty to utter anything before God; for God is in heaven, and you on earth. Therefore let your words be few.
WEB.3: For as a dream comes with a multitude of cares, so a fool’s speech with a multitude of words.
WEB.4: When you vow a vow to God, don’t defer to pay it; for he has no pleasure in fools. Pay that which you vow.
WEB.5: It is better that you should not vow, than that you should vow and not pay.
WEB.6: Don’t allow your mouth to lead you into sin. Don’t protest before the messenger that this was a mistake. Why should God be angry at your voice, and destroy the work of your hands?
WEB.7: For in the multitude of dreams there are vanities, as well as in many words: but you must fear God.
WEB.8: If you see the oppression of the poor, and the violent taking away of justice and righteousness in a district, don’t marvel at the matter: for one official is eyed by a higher one; and there are officials over them.
WEB.9: Moreover the profit of the earth is for all. The king profits from the field.
WEB.10: He who loves silver shall not be satisfied with silver; nor he who loves abundance, with increase: this also is vanity.
WEB.11: When goods increase, those who eat them are increased; and what advantage is there to its owner, except to feast on them with his eyes?
WEB.12: The sleep of a laboring man is sweet, whether he eats little or much; but the abundance of the rich will not allow him to sleep.
WEB.13: There is a grievous evil which I have seen under the sun: wealth kept by its owner to his harm.
WEB.14: Those riches perish by misfortune, and if he has fathered a son, there is nothing in his hand.
WEB.15: As he came out of his mother’s womb, naked shall he go again as he came, and shall take nothing for his labor, which he may carry away in his hand.
WEB.16: This also is a grievous evil, that in all points as he came, so shall he go. And what profit does he have who labors for the wind?
WEB.17: All his days he also eats in darkness, he is frustrated, and has sickness and wrath.
WEB.18: Behold, that which I have seen to be good and proper is for one to eat and to drink, and to enjoy good in all his labor, in which he labors under the sun, all the days of his life which God has given him; for this is his portion.
WEB.19: Every man also to whom God has given riches and wealth, and has given him power to eat of it, and to take his portion, and to rejoice in his labor — this is the gift of God.
WEB.20: For he shall not often reflect on the days of his life; because God occupies him with the joy of his heart.

CSB17.1: Guard your steps when you go to the house of God. Better to approach in obedience than to offer the sacrifice as fools do, <sup>ⓐ</sup> for they ignorantly do wrong.
CSB17.2: Do not be hasty to speak, and do not be impulsive to make a speech before God. God is in heaven and you are on earth, so let your words be few. <sup>ⓑ</sup>
CSB17.3: Just as dreams accompany much labor, so also a fool’s voice comes with many words. <sup>ⓒ</sup>
CSB17.4: When you make a vow to God, <sup>ⓓ</sup> don’t delay fulfilling it, because he does not delight in fools. Fulfill what you vow.
CSB17.5: Better that you do not vow than that you vow and not fulfill it. <sup>ⓔ</sup>
CSB17.6: Do not let your mouth bring guilt on you, <sup>ⓕ</sup> and do not say in the presence of the messenger that it was a mistake. <sup>ⓖ</sup> Why should God be angry with your words and destroy the work of your hands?
CSB17.7: For many dreams bring futility, so do many words. <sup>ⓗ</sup> Therefore, fear God.
CSB17.8: If you see oppression of the poor <sup>ⓘ</sup> and perversion of justice and righteousness in the province, don’t be astonished at the situation, <sup>ⓙ</sup> because one official protects another official, and higher officials protect them.
CSB17.9: The profit from the land is taken by all; the king is served by the field. <sup>[1]</sup> <sup>ⓚ</sup>
CSB17.10: The one who loves silver is never satisfied with silver, and whoever loves wealth is never satisfied with income. This too is futile.
CSB17.11: When good things increase, the ones who consume them multiply; what, then, is the profit to the owner, except to gaze at them with his eyes?
CSB17.12: The sleep of the worker is sweet, whether he eats little or much, but the abundance of the rich permits him no sleep.
CSB17.13: There is a sickening tragedy I have seen under the sun: wealth kept by its owner to his harm. <sup>ⓛ</sup>
CSB17.14: That wealth was lost in a bad venture, so when he fathered a son, he was empty-handed.
CSB17.15: As he came from his mother’s womb, so he will go again, naked as he came; <sup>ⓜ</sup> he will take nothing for his efforts that he can carry in his hands.
CSB17.16: This too is a sickening tragedy: exactly as he comes, so he will go. What does the one gain <sup>ⓝ</sup> who struggles for the wind? <sup>ⓐ</sup>
CSB17.17: What is more, he eats in darkness all his days, <sup>ⓑ</sup> with much frustration, sickness, and anger.
CSB17.18: Here is what I have seen to be good: <sup>ⓒ</sup> It is appropriate to eat, drink, and experience good in all the labor one does under the sun during the few days of his life God has given him, because that is his reward. <sup>ⓓ</sup>
CSB17.19: Furthermore, everyone to whom God has given riches and wealth, <sup>ⓔ</sup> he has also allowed him to enjoy them, take his reward, and rejoice in his labor. <sup>ⓕ</sup> This is a gift of God, <sup>ⓖ</sup>
CSB17.20: for he does not often consider the days of his life because God keeps him occupied with the joy of his heart.

AMP.1: Guard your steps and focus on what you are doing as you go to the house of God and draw near to listen rather than to offer the [careless or irreverent] sacrifice of fools; for they are too ignorant to know they are doing evil.
AMP.2: Do not be hasty with your mouth [speaking careless words or vows] or impulsive in thought to bring up a matter before God. For God is in heaven and you are on earth; therefore let your words be few.
AMP.3: For the dream comes through much effort, and the voice of the fool through many words.
AMP.4: When you make a vow or a pledge to God, do not put off paying it; for God takes no pleasure in fools [who thoughtlessly mock Him]. Pay what you vow.
AMP.5: It is better that you should not vow than that you should vow and not pay.
AMP.6: Do not allow your speech to cause you to sin, and do not say before the messenger (priest) of God that it was a mistake. Why should God be angry because of your voice (words) and destroy the work of your hands?
AMP.7: For in a multitude of dreams and in a flood of words there is worthlessness. Rather [reverently] fear God [and worship Him with awe-filled respect, knowing who He is].
AMP.8: If you see the oppression of the poor and the denial of justice and righteousness in the province, do not be shocked at the sight [of corruption]; for a higher official watches over another official, and there are higher ones over them [looking out for one another].
AMP.9: After all, a king who cultivates the field is an advantage to the land.
AMP.10: He who loves money will not be satisfied with money, nor he who loves abundance with its gain. This too is vanity (emptiness).
AMP.11: When good things increase, those who consume them increase. So what advantage is there to their owners except to see them with their eyes?
AMP.12: The sleep of a working man is sweet, whether he eats little or much; but the full stomach (greed) of the rich [who hungers for even more] will not let him sleep.
AMP.13: There is a grievous evil which I have seen under the sun: riches being kept and hoarded by their owner to his own misery.
AMP.14: For when those riches are lost in bad investments and he becomes the father of a son, then there is nothing in his hand [for the support of the child].
AMP.15: As he came naked from his mother's womb, so he will return as he came; and he will take away nothing from all his labor that he can carry in his hand.
AMP.16: This also is a grievous evil—exactly as he was born, so he shall die. So what advantage has he who labors for the wind?
AMP.17: All of his life he also eats in darkness [cheerlessly, without sweetness and light], with great frustration, sickness, and anger.
AMP.18: Behold, here is what I have seen to be good and fitting: to eat and drink, and to find enjoyment in all the labor in which he labors under the sun during the few days of his life which God gives him—for this is his [allotted] reward.
AMP.19: Also, every man to whom God has given riches and possessions, He has also given the power and ability to enjoy them and to receive [this as] his [allotted] portion and to rejoice in his labor—this is the gift of God [to him].
AMP.20: For he will not often consider the [troubled] days of his life, because God keeps him occupied and focused on the joy of his heart [and the tranquility of God indwells him].

Stand in Awe of God

NIV.2:
Do not be quick with your mouth,
do not be hasty in your heart
to utter anything before God.
God is in heaven
and you are on earth,
so let your words be few.
NIV.3:
As a dream comes when there are many cares,
so the speech of a fool when there are many words.
NIV.4: When you make a vow to God, do not delay in fulfilling it. He has no pleasure in fools; fulfill your vow.
NIV.5: It is better not to vow than to make a vow and not fulfill it.

NIV.7: Much dreaming and many words are meaningless. Therefore stand in awe of God.
NIV.8:
Riches Are Meaningless
If you see the poor oppressed in a district, and justice and rights denied, do not be surprised at such things; for one official is eyed by a higher one, and over them both are others higher still.
NIV.9: The increase from the land is taken by all; the king himself profits from the fields.
NIV.10:
Whoever loves money never has money enough;
whoever loves wealth is never satisfied with his income.
This too is meaningless.
NIV.11:
As goods increase,
so do those who consume them.
And what benefit are they to the owner
except to feast his eyes on them?
NIV.12:
The sleep of a laborer is sweet,
whether he eats little or much,
but the abundance of a rich man
permits him no sleep.
NIV.13:
I have seen a grievous evil under the sun:
wealth hoarded to the harm of its owner,
NIV.14:
or wealth lost through some misfortune,
so that when he has a son
there is nothing left for him.
NIV.15:
Naked a man comes from his mother’s womb,
and as he comes, so he departs.
He takes nothing from his labor
that he can carry in his hand.
NIV.16:
This too is a grievous evil:
As a man comes, so he departs,
and what does he gain,
since he toils for the wind?
NIV.17:
All his days he eats in darkness,
with great frustration, affliction and anger.
NIV.18: Then I realized that it is good and proper for a man to eat and drink, and to find satisfaction in his toilsome labor under the sun during the few days of life God has given him—for this is his lot.
NIV.19: Moreover, when God gives any man wealth and possessions, and enables him to enjoy them, to accept his lot and be happy in his work—this is a gift of God.
NIV.20: He seldom reflects on the days of his life, because God keeps him occupied with gladness of heart.

MSG.1:
Watch your step when you enter God's house.
Enter to learn. That's far better than mindlessly offering
a sacrifice,
Doing more harm than good.
MSG.2:
Don't shoot off your mouth, or speak before you think.
Don't be too quick to tell God what you think he wants to hear.
God's in charge, not you—the less you speak, the better.
MSG.3:
Over-work makes for restless sleep.
Over-talk shows you up as a fool.
MSG.4:
When you tell God you'll do something, do it—now.
God takes no pleasure in foolish gabble. Vow it, then do it.
MSG.5: Far better not to vow in the first place than to vow and not pay up.
MSG.6:
Don't let your mouth make a total sinner of you.
When called to account, you won't get by with
"Sorry, I didn't mean it."
Why risk provoking God to angry retaliation?
MSG.7:
But against all illusion and fantasy and empty talk
There's always this rock foundation: Fear God!
MSG.8: Don't be too upset when you see the poor kicked around, and justice and right violated all over the place. Exploitation filters down from one petty official to another. There's no end to it, and nothing can be done about it.
MSG.9: But the good earth doesn't cheat anyone—even a bad king is honestly served by a field.
MSG.10:
The one who loves money is never satisfied with money,
Nor the one who loves wealth with big profits. More smoke.
MSG.11:
The more loot you get, the more looters show up.
And what fun is that—to be robbed in broad daylight?
MSG.12:
Hard and honest work earns a good night's sleep,
Whether supper is beans or steak.
But a rich man's belly gives him insomnia.
MSG.13:
Here's a piece of bad luck I've seen happen:
A man hoards far more wealth than is good for him
MSG.14:
And then loses it all in a bad business deal.
He fathered a child but hasn't a cent left to give him.
MSG.15:
He arrived naked from the womb of his mother;
He'll leave in the same condition—with nothing.
MSG.16:
This is bad luck, for sure—naked he came, naked he went.
So what was the point of working for a salary of smoke?
MSG.17: All for a miserable life spent in the dark?
MSG.18: After looking at the way things are on this earth, here's what I've decided is the best way to live: Take care of yourself, have a good time, and make the most of whatever job you have for as long as God gives you life. And that's about it. That's the human lot.
MSG.19: Yes, we should make the most of what God gives, both the bounty and the capacity to enjoy it, accepting what's given and delighting in the work. It's God's gift!
MSG.20: God deals out joy in the present, the now. It's useless to brood over how long we might live.

NRSVCE.1: Guard your steps when you go to the house of God; to draw near to listen is better than the sacrifice offered by fools; for they do not know how to keep from doing evil.
NRSVCE.2: Never be rash with your mouth, nor let your heart be quick to utter a word before God, for God is in heaven, and you upon earth; therefore let your words be few.
NRSVCE.3: For dreams come with many cares, and a fool’s voice with many words.
NRSVCE.4: When you make a vow to God, do not delay fulfilling it; for he has no pleasure in fools. Fulfill what you vow.
NRSVCE.5: It is better that you should not vow than that you should vow and not fulfill it.
NRSVCE.6: Do not let your mouth lead you into sin, and do not say before the messenger that it was a mistake; why should God be angry at your words, and destroy the work of your hands?
NRSVCE.7: With many dreams come vanities and a multitude of words; but fear God.
NRSVCE.8: If you see in a province the oppression of the poor and the violation of justice and right, do not be amazed at the matter; for the high official is watched by a higher, and there are yet higher ones over them.
NRSVCE.9: But all things considered, this is an advantage for a land: a king for a plowed field.
NRSVCE.10: The lover of money will not be satisfied with money; nor the lover of wealth, with gain. This also is vanity.
NRSVCE.11: When goods increase, those who eat them increase; and what gain has their owner but to see them with his eyes?
NRSVCE.12: Sweet is the sleep of laborers, whether they eat little or much; but the surfeit of the rich will not let them sleep.
NRSVCE.13: There is a grievous ill that I have seen under the sun: riches were kept by their owners to their hurt,
NRSVCE.14: and those riches were lost in a bad venture; though they are parents of children, they have nothing in their hands.
NRSVCE.15: As they came from their mother’s womb, so they shall go again, naked as they came; they shall take nothing for their toil, which they may carry away with their hands.
NRSVCE.16: This also is a grievous ill: just as they came, so shall they go; and what gain do they have from toiling for the wind?
NRSVCE.17: Besides, all their days they eat in darkness, in much vexation and sickness and resentment.
NRSVCE.18: This is what I have seen to be good: it is fitting to eat and drink and find enjoyment in all the toil with which one toils under the sun the few days of the life God gives us; for this is our lot.
NRSVCE.19: Likewise all to whom God gives wealth and possessions and whom he enables to enjoy them, and to accept their lot and find enjoyment in their toil — this is the gift of God.
NRSVCE.20: For they will scarcely brood over the days of their lives, because God keeps them occupied with the joy of their hearts.

NET.1: Be careful what you do when you go to the temple of God; draw near to listen rather than to offer a sacrifice like fools, for they do not realize that they are doing wrong.
NET.2: Do not be rash with your mouth or hasty in your heart to bring up a matter before God, for God is in heaven and you are on earth! Therefore, let your words be few.
NET.3: Just as dreams come when there are many cares, so the rash vow of a fool occurs when there are many words.
NET.4: When you make a vow to God, do not delay in paying it. For God takes no pleasure in fools: Pay what you vow!
NET.5: It is better for you not to vow than to vow and not pay it.
NET.6: Do not let your mouth cause you to sin, and do not tell the priest, “It was a mistake!” Why make God angry at you so that he would destroy the work of your hands?”
NET.7: Just as there is futility in many dreams, so also in many words. Therefore, fear God!
NET.8: If you see the extortion of the poor, or the perversion of justice and fairness in the government, do not be astonished by the matter. For the high official is watched by a higher official, and there are higher ones over them!
NET.9: The produce of the land is seized by all of them, even the king is served by the fields.
NET.10: The one who loves money will never be satisfied with money, he who loves wealth will never be satisfied with his income. This also is futile.
NET.11: When someone’s prosperity increases, those who consume it also increase; so what does its owner gain, except that he gets to see it with his eyes?
NET.12: The sleep of the laborer is pleasant — whether he eats little or much — but the wealth of the rich will not allow him to sleep.
NET.13: Here is a misfortune on earth that I have seen: Wealth hoarded by its owner to his own misery.
NET.14: Then that wealth was lost through bad luck; although he fathered a son, he has nothing left to give him.
NET.15: Just as he came forth from his mother's womb, naked will he return as he came, and he will take nothing in his hand that he may carry away from his toil.
NET.16: This is another misfortune: Just as he came, so will he go. What did he gain from toiling for the wind?
NET.17: Surely, he ate in darkness every day of his life, and he suffered greatly with sickness and anger.
NET.18: I have seen personally what is the only beneficial and appropriate course of action for people: to eat and drink, and find enjoyment in all their hard work on earth during the few days of their life which God has given them, for this is their reward.
NET.19: To every man whom God has given wealth, and possessions, he has also given him the ability to eat from them, to receive his reward and to find enjoyment in his toil; these things are the gift of God.
NET.20: For he does not think much about the fleeting days of his life because God keeps him preoccupied with the joy he derives from his activity.
